Dogs with fearful and/or aggressive behavior may not receive adequate veterinary care including wellness care, diagnostics, and treatment.
Effective implementation of Fear Free, Low Stress care prevents and reduces fear, anxiety, and stress and improves frequency and quality of veterinary care.

Dogs with fearful/fractious behavior in veterinary setting often have comorbid behavioral problems, including aggression to owners or strangers, leash reactivity, resource guarding, anxiety disorders.
Socialization period (3–12 weeks)—sensitive period where positive exposure minimizes fear; gentle, brief handling paired with positive experience (food) leads to less fear and improved
Fear period (8–10 weeks of age and between 4 and 11 months)—susceptible to single-event learning, highly sensitive to negative

Social maturity (1–3 years)— fearful puppies/adolescents may begin to show fear and aggression at this time; prompt recognition and intervention essential at first signs of fear to establish handling plan.
